omission_flags: The analysis omits any medical or demographic exploration of why the diabetes rate fell, choosing instead to treat the finding as a lagging indicator.
evasion_flags: Does not address a possible cause of the diabetes decline, pivoting to obesity.

cardinal_sin_flags.quote: A health system can lower a diabetes number for a year. It cannot outrun a population that grows heavier at every survey.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Implies a one-year artificial lowering without evidence the rate was suppressed.
cardinal_sin_flags.fix: While the diabetes rate has shown a decline, the rising obesity rate indicates the underlying risk factors remain unaddressed.

cardinal_sin_flags.why: If 15.6% of adults equals 3.6 million (per NHMS 2023), the adult baseline is roughly 23 million; 54.4% of 23 million is 12.5 million, so 11 million is inconsistent.

verification_log.claim: Adult diabetes fell to 15.6% in 2023, down from 18.3% in 2019
verification_log.primary_source: NHMS 2023 Key Findings / MOH Press Release 16 May 2024

verification_log.claim: Overweight and obesity climbed to 54.4% (2023), up from 50.1% (2019), 47.7% (2015), 44.5% (2011)
Two in five Malaysians with diabetes do not know they have it
Among those aged 18 to 29, about 84% are unaware
One in two adults lead sedentary lives
about 84% take part in no sport, fitness or leisure activity

overall_assessment: Bias score 15. NHMS core data points are accurate; the 11 million obesity figure is mathematically inconsistent with the adult population baseline and should be corrected or dropped.
